vsm1.4:1.2: After that he should avoid a monastery unfavourable to the development of concentration
vsm1.4:1.3: and go to live in one that is favourable (III.28).
vsm1.4:1.4: In the first place one who finds it convenient to live with the teacher in the same monastery
vsm1.4:1.5: can live there while he is making certain of the meditation subject.
vsm1.4:1.6: If it is inconvenient there, he can live in another monastery—a suitable one—a quarter or a half or even a whole league distant.
vsm1.4:1.7: In that case, when he finds he is in doubt about, or has forgotten, some passage in the meditation subject,
vsm1.4:1.8: then he should do the duties in the monastery in good time and set out afterwards,
vsm1.4:1.9: going for alms on the way
vsm1.4:1.10: and arriving at the teacher’s dwelling place after his meal.
vsm1.4:1.11: He should make certain about the meditation subject that day in the teacher’s presence.
vsm1.4:1.12: Next day, after paying homage to the teacher,
vsm1.4:1.13: he should go for alms on his way back
vsm1.4:1.14: and so he can return to his own dwelling place without fatigue.
vsm1.4:1.15: But one who finds no convenient place within even a league
vsm1.4:1.16: should clarify all difficulties about the meditation subject
vsm1.4:1.17: and make quite sure it has been properly attended to.
vsm1.4:1.18: Then he can even go far away and,
vsm1.4:1.19: avoiding a monastery unfavourable to development of concentration,
vsm1.4:1.20: live in one that is favourable.
vsm1.4:2.0: The Eighteen Faults of a Monastery
vsm1.4:2.1: Herein, one that is unfavourable has anyone of eighteen faults.
vsm1.4:2.2: These are: (1) largeness, (2) newness, (3) dilapidatedness, (4) a nearby road,
vsm1.4:2.3: (5) a pond, (6) edible leaves, (7) flowers, (8) fruits, (9) famousness,
vsm1.4:2.4: (10) a nearby city, (11) nearby timber trees, (12) nearby arable fields, (13) presence of incompatible persons,
vsm1.4:2.5: (14) a nearby port of entry, (15) nearness to the border countries, (16) nearness to the frontier of a kingdom,
vsm1.4:2.7: One with any of these faults is not favourable.
vsm1.4:3.1: Firstly, people with varying aims collect in a large monastery.
vsm1.4:3.2: They conflict with each other and so neglect the duties.
vsm1.4:3.3: The Enlightenment-tree terrace, etc., remain unswept, the water for drinking and washing is not set out.
vsm1.4:3.4: So if he thinks, “I shall go to the alms-resort village for alms” and takes his bowl and robe and sets out,
vsm1.4:3.5: perhaps he sees that the duties have not been done or that a drinking-water pot is empty,
vsm1.4:3.6: and so the duty has to be done by him unexpectedly.
vsm1.4:3.8: By not doing it he would commit a wrongdoing in the breach of a duty.
vsm1.4:3.9: But if he does it, he loses time.
vsm1.4:3.10: He arrives too late at the village and gets nothing because the alms giving is finished.
vsm1.4:3.11: Also, when he goes into retreat,
vsm1.4:3.12: he is distracted by the loud noises of novices and young bhikkhus,
vsm1.4:3.13: and by acts of the Community being carried out.
vsm1.4:3.14: However, he can live in a large monastery where all the duties are done and where there are none of the other disturbances.
vsm1.4:4.1: In a new monastery there is much new building activity.
vsm1.4:4.2: People criticize someone who takes no part in it.
vsm1.4:4.3: But he can live in such a monastery where the bhikkhus say,
vsm1.4:4.4: “Let the venerable one do the ascetic’s duties as much as he likes.
vsm1.4:4.5: We shall see to the building work.”
vsm1.4:5.1: In a dilapidated monastery there is much that needs repair.
vsm1.4:5.2: People criticize someone who does not see about the repairing of at least his own lodging.
vsm1.4:5.3: When he sees to the repairs, his meditation subject suffers.
vsm1.4:6.1: In a monastery with a nearby road, by a main street, visitors keep arriving night and day.
vsm1.4:6.2: He has to give up his own lodging to those who come late, and he has to go and live at the root of a tree or on top of a rock.
vsm1.4:6.3: And next day it is the same. So there is no opportunity to practice his meditation subject.
vsm1.4:6.4: But he can live in one where there is no such disturbance by visitors.
vsm1.4:7.1: A pond is a rock pool.
vsm1.4:7.2: Numbers of people come there for drinking water.
vsm1.4:7.3: Pupils of city-dwelling elders supported by the royal family come to do dyeing work.
vsm1.4:7.4: When they ask for vessels, wood, tubs, etc., they must be shown where these things are.
vsm1.4:7.5: So he is kept all the time on the alert.
vsm1.4:8.1: If he goes with his meditation subject to sit by day where there are many sorts of edible leaves,
vsm1.4:8.2: then women vegetable-gatherers, singing as they pick leaves nearby,
vsm1.4:8.3: endanger his meditation subject by disturbing it with sounds of the opposite sex.
vsm1.4:8.4: And where there are many sorts of flowering shrubs in bloom there is the same danger too.
vsm1.4:9.1: Where there are many sorts of fruits such as mangoes, rose-apples and jak-fruits,
vsm1.4:9.2: people who want fruits come and ask for them,
vsm1.4:9.3: and they get angry if he does not give them any,
vsm1.4:9.4: or they take them by force.
vsm1.4:9.5: When walking in the monastery in the evening he sees them and asks,
vsm1.4:9.6: “Why do you do so, lay followers?”
vsm1.4:9.7: they abuse him as they please
vsm1.4:9.8: and even try to evict him.
vsm1.4:10.1: When he lives in a monastery that is famous and renowned in the world, like Dakkhiṇagiri Hatthikucchi, Cetiyagiri or Cittalapabbata,
vsm1.4:10.2: there are always people coming who want to pay homage to him, supposing that he is an Arahant,
vsm1.4:10.4: But if it suits him, he can live there at night and go elsewhere by day.
vsm1.4:11.1: In one with a nearby city objects of the opposite sex come into focus.
vsm1.4:11.2: Women-pot carriers go by bumping into him with their jars and giving no room to pass.
vsm1.4:11.3: Also important people spread out carpets in the middle of the monastery and sit down.
vsm1.4:12.1: One with nearby timber trees where there are timber trees and osiers useful for making framework
vsm1.4:12.2: is inconvenient because of the wood-gatherers there, like the gatherers of branches and fruits already mentioned.
vsm1.4:12.3: If there are trees in a monastery, people come and cut them down to build houses with.
vsm1.4:12.4: When he has come out of his meditation room in the evening
vsm1.4:12.5: and is walking up and down in the monastery, if he sees them
vsm1.4:12.6: and asks, “Why do you do so, lay followers?”
vsm1.4:12.7: they abuse him as they please
vsm1.4:12.8: and even try to evict him.
vsm1.4:13.1: People make use of one with nearby arable fields, quite surrounded by fields.
vsm1.4:13.2: They make a threshing floor in the middle of the monastery itself. They thresh corn there,
vsm1.4:13.5: And where there is extensive property belonging to the Community,
vsm1.4:13.6: the monastery attendants impound cattle belonging to families
vsm1.4:13.7: and deny the water supply to their crops.
vsm1.4:13.8: Then people bring an ear of paddy and show it to the Community saying “Look at your monastery attendants’ work.”
vsm1.4:13.9: For one reason or another he has to go to the portals of the king or the king’s ministers.
vsm1.4:13.10: This matter of property belonging to the Community is included by a monastery that is near arable fields.
vsm1.4:14.1: Presence of incompatible persons: where there are bhikkhus living who are incompatible and mutually hostile,
vsm1.4:14.2: when they clash and it is protested,
vsm1.4:14.4: they exclaim, “We no longer count now that this refuse-rag wearer has come.”
vsm1.4:15.1: One with a nearby water port of entry or land port of entry
vsm1.4:15.2: is made inconvenient by people constantly arriving respectively by ship or by caravan
vsm1.4:15.3: and crowding round, asking for space or for drinking water or salt.
vsm1.4:16.1: In the case of one near the border countries, people have no trust in the Buddha, etc., there.
vsm1.4:16.2: In one near the frontier of a kingdom there is fear of kings.
vsm1.4:16.3: For perhaps one king attacks that place, thinking, “It does not submit to my rule,”
vsm1.4:16.4: and the other does likewise, thinking, “It does not submit to my rule.”
vsm1.4:16.5: A bhikkhu lives there when it is conquered by one king and when it is conquered by the other.
vsm1.4:16.6: Then they suspect him of spying, and they bring about his undoing.
vsm1.4:17.1: Unsuitability is that due to the risk of encountering visible data, etc., of the opposite sex as objects
vsm1.4:17.2: or to haunting by non-human beings.
vsm1.4:17.4: An elder lived in a forest, it seems.
vsm1.4:17.5: Then an ogress stood in the door of his leaf hut and sang.
vsm1.4:17.6: The elder came out and stood in the door.
vsm1.4:17.7: She went to the end of the walk and sang.
vsm1.4:17.8: The elder went to the end of the walk.
vsm1.4:17.9: She stood in a chasm a hundred fathoms deep and sang.
vsm1.4:17.11: Then she suddenly grabbed him saying, “Venerable sir, it is not just one or two of the likes of you I have eaten.”
vsm1.4:18.2: where it is not possible to find a good friend as a teacher or the equivalent of a teacher
vsm1.4:18.3: or a preceptor or the equivalent of a preceptor,
vsm1.4:18.4: the lack of good friends there is a serious fault.
vsm1.4:18.5: One that has any of those eighteen faults should be understood as unfavourable.
vsm1.4:18.6: And this is said in the commentaries:
vsm1.4:18.7:
A large abode, a new abode,
One tumbling down, one near a road,
vsm1.4:18.8:
One with a pond, or leaves, or flowers,
Or fruits, or one that people seek;
vsm1.4:18.9:
In cities, among timber, fields,
Where people quarrel, in a port,
vsm1.4:18.10:
In border lands, on frontiers,
Unsuitableness, and no good friend—
vsm1.4:18.11:
These are the eighteen instances
A wise man needs to recognize
And give them full as wide a berth
As any footpad-hunted road.
vsm1.4:19.0: The Five Factors of the Resting Place
vsm1.4:19.1: One that has the five factors beginning with “not too far from and not too near to” the alms resort is called favourable.
vsm1.4:19.2: For this is said by the Blessed One: “And how has a lodging five factors, bhikkhus?
vsm1.4:19.3: Here, bhikkhus, (1) a lodging is not too far, not too near, and has a path for going and coming.
vsm1.4:19.4: (2) It is little frequented by day with little sound and few voices by night.
vsm1.4:19.5: (3) There is little contact with gadflies, flies, wind, burning sun and creeping things.
vsm1.4:19.6: (4) One who lives in that lodging easily obtains robes, alms food, lodging, and the requisite of medicine as cure for the sick.
vsm1.4:19.7: (5) In that lodging there are elder bhikkhus living who are learned, versed in the scriptures,
vsm1.4:19.8: observers of the Dhamma, observers of the Vinaya, observers of the Codes,
vsm1.4:19.9: and when from time to time one asks them questions, ‘How is this, venerable sir? What is the meaning of this?’
vsm1.4:19.10: then those venerable ones reveal the unrevealed,
vsm1.4:19.12: and remove doubt about the many things that raise doubts.
vsm1.4:19.13: This, bhikkhus, is how a lodging has five factors” (A V 15).
vsm1.4:19.14: These are the details for the clause, “After that he should avoid a monastery unfavourable to the development of concentration
vsm1.4:19.15: and go to live in one that is favourable” (III.28).
vsm1.4:20.1: Then he should sever the lesser impediments (III.28):
vsm1.4:20.2: one living in such a favourable monastery
vsm1.4:20.3: should sever any minor impediments that he may still have,
vsm1.4:20.4: that is to say, long head hair, nails, and body hair should be cut,
vsm1.4:20.5: mending and patching of old robes should be done,
vsm1.4:20.6: or those that are soiled should be dyed.
vsm1.4:20.7: If there is a stain on the bowl, the bowl should be baked.
vsm1.4:20.8: The bed, chair, etc., should be cleaned up.
vsm1.4:20.9: These are the details for the clause, “Then he should sever the lesser impediments.”
